title: Set sheafification commutes with localization compatibly with its unit
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $A,U$ etale objects [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $f:A\to U$ a morphism in the small etale site, and $J=Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Put $L=\operatorname{Over.map}(f):\operatorname{Over}(A)\to\operatorname{Over}(U)$. For every set presheaf $P$ on $\operatorname{Over}(U)$ there is a canonical sheaf isomorphism between the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $L^{\mathrm{op}}P$ on $J/A$ and the restriction along $L$ of the sheafification of $P$ on $J/U$. The unit on $J/A$ followed by its underlying presheaf map equals the restriction of the unit on $J/U$. In particular this identifies the restriction of the constant set sheaf at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] with the constant sheaf at $S$ on $J/A$. For any set sheaf $H$ on $J$, the restriction along $L$ of $H|_U$ is canonically isomorphic to $H|_A$, with identity maps on each section set.

proof.text: Over.map f is continuous and cocontinuous for the over topologies (Over.lean instances at lines 323 and 328). Apply pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility to Type-valued presheaves; all Kan extensions and sheafification instances are supplied by the existing site instances. Its unit formula is toSheafify_pullbackSheafificationCompatibility. Specializing to a constant presheaf gives the constant-sheaf case. The final restriction identification is Sheaf.pushforwardOverMapIso, whose components are identity isomorphisms.
